content_html:
Before your next call or selfie, the Live Filter Preview lets you see what brightness, contrast, saturation and blur do to your webcam image side by side with the untouched feed. Unlike novelty webcam effects, these are tonal real-time effects, so you get a clear before-and-after answer on how to fix a dim or washed-out camera in seconds, for free.

How the Live Filter Preview Works

Click Start Camera, pick a device if you have more than one camera input, then drag the four sliders. Everything runs online with no installation and no plugin, and when the look is right you can download a still photo and save it to your computer.

Allow Access to Your Web Camera

Your browser asks once for permission; choose allow access or the web camera stays dark. There is no registration, and for privacy the stream is processed locally on your devices, never uploaded.

A Real Time Before and After Mirror

The left pane shows the raw feed and the right pane shows the filtered one, updated in real time like a mirror. If your image looks flipped or upside-down, that comes from the camera driver, not from the filters, and it affects all your photos.

Brightness, Contrast and Saturation: The Webcam Filters Explained

The four webcam filters are deliberately simple filter options that correct a photo rather than decorate it. Turn saturation to 0% and you get a true black and white picture; nothing here adds grainy texture or colour casts.

SliderRangeWhat it changes
Brightness50–150%Multiplies every channel; lifts a dark room
Contrast50–150%Pushes tones away from mid-grey
Saturation0–200%0% gives black & white, 200% doubles colour
Blur0–10 pxSoftens fine detail

The Formulas Behind Each Slider

Each slider applies the standard CSS filter maths to every pixel channel \(C\) (0–255), in this order: brightness, contrast, saturation, blur. No computer vision is involved.

$$C_{b} = C \times b \qquad C_{c} = (C - 127.5) \times c + 127.5$$ $$R_{s} = (0.213 + 0.787s)R + (0.715 - 0.715s)G + (0.072 - 0.072s)B$$

Saturation keeps luminance fixed while moving each channel toward or away from grey, which is why these effects and filters never change how bright you look.

Blur for Skin Smoothing and Touch-Ups

A 1–2 px blur gives a soft focus that hides texture, a crude version of the skin smoothing in beauty filters. It cannot add makeup or targeted touch-ups, and above 4 px it looks like bokeh on your face.

Take Photos Online With Live Filters: A Worked Example

Say your desk lamp sits behind the screen and a cheek pixel reads RGB(148, 104, 86), luminance 112.1. You set brightness 118%, contrast 106% and saturation 88% with live filters:

StepCheek pixelWall pixel
Original148, 104, 8671, 74, 83
Brightness 118%174.6, 122.7, 101.583.8, 87.3, 97.9
Contrast 106%177.5, 122.4, 99.981.2, 84.9, 96.2
Saturation 88%172, 124, 10482, 85, 95

Your skin's luminance rises from 112.1 to 132.5, while contrast pulls the darker wall back down by 2.4 levels, so you separate from the background. The 88% saturation trims the orange lamp cast without the flat look of vintage filters. One caveat: at 118% any channel above 216 clips to 255, so check a bright window before you take photos online with these settings. That does more for your confidence than any aesthetic preset.

Balancing a Window-Lit Tutoring Call With Webcam Effects

A maths tutor has a parent meeting at 4:15 on a laptop whose desk faces a north window. The question is simple: which brightness and contrast settings make both sides of the face readable without blowing out the lit side? The answer turns out to be brightness 112%, contrast 94% and saturation 104%, and the filter preview shows why before the call starts.

With the camera running, the tutor samples two spots from a downloaded still: the window-side forehead at RGB(203, 171, 152), luminance 176.4, and the shadow-side cheek at RGB(97, 72, 63), luminance 76.7. That 99.8-level gap is what makes the face look half lit.

The first instinct is brightness alone. At 112% the shadow cheek lifts to luminance 85.9, but the gap widens to 111.7, because brightness multiplies every value and bright values gain more. Dropping contrast to 94% pulls both sides toward mid-grey and brings the gap back to 105.0, with the shadow cheek at 88.4 and the forehead at 193.4. Saturation at 104% only restores a little warmth that the grey window light drains; it leaves luminance where it is.

SettingsForehead redLight/shadow gap
No filters203.099.8
112% / 100% / 104%228.5111.7
112% / 94% / 104%222.5105.0
120% / 94% / 104%237.8112.5

The cross-check is the broadcast video range in ITU-R BT.709, where 235 is reference white. Solving the same formulas for the forehead red channel shows it crosses 235 at about 119% brightness, so 120% is already past the point where compression in a meeting app tends to flatten skin into a white patch. That is the number to watch here, not the shadow side.

The caveat: this webcam filter preview only shows the result locally. The tutor's next step is to enter brightness +12 and contrast −6 in the camera's own settings, then rerun the preview at neutral sliders to confirm the raw feed now matches. If the window brightens later in the day, the forehead crosses 235 sooner, so a lamp on the shadow side fixes the gap more reliably than any slider.

Live Effects vs Photo Booth Filters, AR Lenses and Masks

An online photo booth or a webcam toy layers fun effects and digital effects on top of the image. AR lenses and AR effects use augmented reality to track your face and pin masks, hairstyles, glasses, hats or beards to it. The photo booth approach is for play; tonal filters make you look better lit.

Photo Booth Effects and Distorting Styles

Most photo booth effects fall into a few families; the right column shows what these camera filters for tone can match:

FamilyExamplesWith these sliders
Colour looksvintage, old movie, rainbow, underwater, pop art, watercolor, sketch, comic bookMuted or mono looks only
Simulated sensorsnight vision, thermal, x-rayNo
Warpsfisheye, bulge, pinch, twist, ripple, kaleidoscopeNo
Layoutssplit screen, quad camNo
Face trackingreal-time masksNo

Frames and Stickers on a Photo Strip

Here you save one still with no frames or stickers. Booth tools take four pictures about 3 seconds apart, decorate them and let you share the photo strip; a photo booth camera is built to take pictures online for fun, record videos or make GIF animations, while this preview checks selfies or a video setup.

Camera Filters for Video Calls and Streaming

For video calls and streaming, find your brightness, contrast and saturation values here, then enter them in Zoom, OBS or Discord. A virtual camera adds what this page cannot: a webcam beauty filter, a former Snap Camera lens, live effects such as neon or glitch, or a beauty filter on every frame.

Why a Preview Is Not a Virtual Camera

The Live Filter Preview never touches the feed other apps receive. Use it to find your numbers, then copy them into your meeting app or free webcam filters that do run real-time effects on the transmitted stream.

Online Camera in Any Browser on Laptop, Tablet and Phone

This online camera is cross-platform and mobile-friendly: it works in Chrome, Edge and other browsers on a desktop, laptop, tablet or phone. If it fails to start, close other apps using the camera.

faq.question: How much does the live filter preview cost?
faq.answer: Nothing. The webcam filters run free in your browser, with no account, no registration and no limit on how many stills you download.

faq.question: Do I need to install anything to use these webcam filters?
faq.answer: No. There is no installation and no plugin; the preview runs in Chrome, Edge and other current browsers on a laptop, desktop, tablet or phone.

faq.question: Why does my camera not show up?
faq.answer: Your browser has to be allowed to use the camera. Click Start Camera, choose allow access when asked, and close any other app (Zoom, Teams, OBS) that may already be holding the camera.

faq.question: Does the preview change what people see in my video calls?
faq.answer: No. It only filters the copy shown on this page. To use the look in a call, copy the brightness, contrast and saturation values into your meeting app or camera settings, or use a virtual camera app.

faq.question: Can I add stickers, frames or fun effects?
faq.answer: Not here. Photo booth tools add frames, stickers, AR masks and novelty effects such as fisheye or night vision; this tool sticks to tonal adjustments so you look natural, just better lit.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded anywhere?
faq.answer: No. The camera stream is processed locally in your browser and the downloaded still is saved straight to your device.

faq.question: Which settings fix a dark webcam image?
faq.answer: Start by raising brightness to around 110-120% and check that bright areas such as a window do not clip, then adjust contrast a few points either way and trim saturation if a lamp gives your skin an orange cast.
